precepts.text: John shall drink neither wine nor strong drink, filled with the Holy Ghost from the womb, going before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elias to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
precepts.point: John was filled with the Holy Spirit before he was born, and Elizabeth did not sleep with an angel; Zacharias was her husband. The same way Christ was filled with the Holy Spirit before birth; the immaculate conception is a Catholic doctrine, not the scriptures.

note.label: Numbers 6: The Law of the Nazarite and the Blessing of Israel

precepts.why:
The Nazarite separated himself unto the Lord “from wine and strong drink”, drank no vinegar of wine nor liquor of grapes, and ate nothing made of the vine tree, from the kernels even to the husk. John the Baptist fell under that Nazarite vow. The angel told Zacharias, “thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John”, and “he shall be great in the sight of the Lord, and shall drink neither wine nor strong drink; and he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother’s womb.”

John was filled with the Holy Spirit before he was born. Elizabeth did not sleep with an angel; Zacharias was her husband. The same way Christ was filled with the Holy Spirit before birth; the immaculate conception is a Catholic doctrine, not the scriptures.

“And many of the children of Israel shall he turn to the Lord their God. And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.” A Nazarite from the womb, going before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elias.

precepts.text: Samson spoke of the seven locks of his head; the locks of the Nazarite mark the man the scripture describes.
precepts.point: Samson was a Nazarite also, from the tribe of Dan; he got caught up in wickedness with the daughters of Ham, but he was a Nazarite, and his hair grew in seven locks. That description is not speaking of the people who call themselves Jews today, whatever the movies portray.

note.label: Numbers 6: The Law of the Nazarite and the Blessing of Israel

precepts.why:
All the days of the vow “there shall no razor come upon his head”; he was holy, and let the locks of the hair of his head grow. Samson was a Nazarite also, from the tribe of Dan. He got caught up in wickedness with the daughters of Ham, but he was a Nazarite, and his hair grew in seven locks.

“And Delilah said unto Samson, Hitherto thou hast mocked me, and told me lies: tell me wherewith thou mightest be bound. And he said unto her, If thou weavest the seven locks of my head with the web.”

The seven locks of his head are the locks of the Nazarite, and they mark the man the scripture describes. That description is not speaking of the people who call themselves Jews today, whatever the movies portray.

precepts.text: Unto the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain the Jews; that is why Paul took the charges of the vow.
precepts.point: The elders at Jerusalem told Paul to purify himself with four men which had a vow on them and be at charges with them, that all may know thou thyself walkest orderly and keepest the law. And note it well: the thousands there that believed were Jews, all zealous of the law, and the Gentiles Paul taught among were Jews scattered among the Gentiles.

note.label: Numbers 6: The Law of the Nazarite and the Blessing of Israel

precepts.why:
When a Nazarite’s separation was defiled by the dead, he shaved his head on the seventh day, brought two turtles or two young pigeons on the eighth day and a lamb of the first year for a trespass offering, and the days before were lost. Paul partook in that Nazarite purification.

“And unto the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain the Jews; to them that are under the law, as under the law, that I might gain them that are under the law.”

Unto the Jews he became a Jew; he brought himself down to their level of understanding to win them over, not by breaking the law but by walking orderly and keeping it. That is why Paul took the charges of the vow.

precepts.text: Thousands of Jews which believe, all zealous of the law, and Jews among the Gentiles; Paul purified himself with the four men that had a vow, walking orderly and keeping the law.
precepts.point: The elders at Jerusalem told Paul to purify himself with four men which had a vow on them and be at charges with them, that all may know thou thyself walkest orderly and keepest the law. And note it well: the thousands there that believed were Jews, all zealous of the law, and the Gentiles Paul taught among were Jews scattered among the Gentiles.

note.label: Numbers 6: The Law of the Nazarite and the Blessing of Israel

precepts.why:
The elders at Jerusalem told Paul: “Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law: And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.”

Note it well: the thousands there that believed were Jews, all zealous of the law, and the Gentiles Paul taught among were Jews scattered among the Gentiles.

“Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men which have a vow on them; Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.” The shaving of the head and the charges of the offering are the Nazarite purification of Numbers 6. Paul purified himself with the four men that had a vow, walking orderly and keeping the law.

precepts.text: Take, eat, this is my body; this cup is the new testament in my blood, this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me. The cup of the covenant is why the Nazarite vow cannot be kept under Christ.
precepts.point: After that the Nazarite may drink wine; before that he could not. In our understanding today you cannot keep the vow of a Nazarite under Christ: you can let your hair grow as long as you want, but when we break bread and take the cup in remembrance of Christ, renewing that covenant, you have to drink that wine to be in covenant with him.

note.label: Numbers 6: The Law of the Nazarite and the Blessing of Israel

precepts.why:
When the days of his separation were fulfilled, the Nazarite offered a he lamb and a ewe lamb “without blemish”, the same thing going into Christ, with unleavened bread and the meat and drink offerings; he shaved the head of his separation and put the hair in the fire under the peace offerings, and the priest waved the sodden shoulder and the cakes before the Lord. Then “after that the Nazarite may drink wine”; before that he could not.

In our understanding today you cannot keep the vow of a Nazarite under Christ. Paul delivered what he received: “That the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread: And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me. After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.”

You can let your hair grow as long as you want, but when we break bread and take the cup in remembrance of Christ, renewing that covenant, you have to drink that wine to be in covenant with him. The cup of the covenant is why the Nazarite vow cannot be kept under Christ.

precepts.text: Because your fathers have forsaken me and walked after other gods, and ye have done worse than your fathers, therefore will I cast you out of this land into a land that ye know not, where I will not shew you favour.
precepts.point: The Most High has taken that blessing from us, and we have to work to get it back by repentance and enduring to the end. But it will happen again; the Lord is pulling his spirit back out on us, and the remnant is waking up.

note.label: Numbers 6: The Law of the Nazarite and the Blessing of Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord bless thee, and keep thee: The Lord make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: The Lord lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.” All of that is a stipulation, a contract; it is not unconditional love with the Most High. Keep my commandments and live.

When the southern kingdom asked, “Wherefore hath the Lord pronounced all this great evil against us? or what is our iniquity? or what is our sin that we have committed against the Lord our God?”, the answer was: “Because your fathers have forsaken me, saith the Lord, and have walked after other gods, and have served them, and have worshipped them, and have forsaken me, and have not kept my law; And ye have done worse than your fathers; for, behold, ye walk every one after the imagination of his evil heart, that they may not hearken unto me.”

Bring it up to today: Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, Hinduism, every denomination walking after the imagination of its own evil heart. “Therefore will I cast you out of this land into a land that ye know not, neither ye nor your fathers; and there shall ye serve other gods day and night; where I will not shew you favour.” Cast out into a land we knew not, serving gods where the Lord shows no favor: that is why our people have no peace and no blessing.

The Most High has taken that blessing from us, and we have to work to get it back by repentance and enduring to the end. But it will happen again; the Lord is pulling his spirit back out on us, and the remnant is waking up.

precepts.text: When a man or woman separates themselves to vow a vow of a Nazarite, they are on another level of dedication to the Lord: no wine, no strong drink, no vinegar, no liquor of grapes, nothing made of the vine tree from the kernels even to the husk.
precepts.point: The locks of the Nazarite also witness to who Israel is; the hair of Israel naturally grows into locks.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

precepts.why:
The angel commanded the mother herself to “drink not wine nor strong drink, and eat not any unclean thing”, because “the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb”; even in the womb he was to be kept pure. The vow is laid out in Numbers 6: “When either man or woman shall separate themselves to vow a vow of a Nazarite, to separate themselves unto the Lord: He shall separate himself from wine and strong drink, and shall drink no vinegar of wine, or vinegar of strong drink, neither shall he drink any liquor of grapes, nor eat moist grapes, or dried.” Nothing made of the vine tree, “from the kernels even to the husk.” A Nazarite is on another level of dedication to the Lord.

Samson is one of the first examples in scripture of somebody actually living that vow. Understand the difference between a Nazarite and a Nazarene: Christ was a Nazarene because he was from the city of Nazareth, not a Nazarite; he drank wine, and Nazarites could not drink the blood of the grape at all.

precepts.text: All the days of the vow no razor shall come upon his head; he shall be holy and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow, which is why the angel gave Manoah's wife these instructions.
precepts.point: The locks of the Nazarite also witness to who Israel is; the hair of Israel naturally grows into locks.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

precepts.why:
“no razor shall come on his head: for the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb”. That comes straight from the vow: “All the days of the vow of his separation there shall no razor come upon his head: until the days be fulfilled, in the which he separateth himself unto the Lord, he shall be holy, and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow.” That is why the angel gave Manoah’s wife these instructions; her son’s days of separation would run from the womb, and he would begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.

The locks of the Nazarite also witness to who Israel is: the hair of Israel naturally grows into locks, the locks the vow speaks of.

precepts.text: All the days of the vow of his separation no rasor comes upon his head; he shall be holy, and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow.
precepts.point: She vowed a vow: O Lord of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the Lord all the days of his life, and there shall no rasor come upon his head. What law is that going back to? The law of the Nazarite. Put some things together as you read through Samuel about Samuel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

precepts.why:
“All the days of the vow of his separation there shall no razor come upon his head: until the days be fulfilled, in the which he separateth himself unto the Lord, he shall be holy, and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow.”

Hannah, in bitterness of soul, vowed: if the Lord would “give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the Lord all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.” What law is that going back to? The law of the Nazarite. Put that together as you read through Samuel about Samuel: he was given to the Lord under the Nazarite vow.

The locks of a Nazarite are hair braided so that it locks into place as it grows long. When you braid your hair, you are locking it in.
